reconcile_note: Terminal not-vulnerable. Blind verdict was need-more-context because the decompiler renders the command site as a wrapper call Antivirus_Engine(&buf, "...scan %d...", jobid) then system(&buf); from the body alone one cannot tell whether that wrapper reads stored job config strings into buf. The single on-target (raw disasm at 0x0001f416) resolves this: the site is not a wrapper, it is an inline sprintf(buf, fmt@0x3eb98, jobid) followed by system(buf), where the only variadic operand is the integer job id (r5) formatted with %d, and a second system runs the fixed constant at 0x3ebc8. Since buf is built only from a constant template plus one integer, no attacker string can reach the command. That one artifact is independently necessary and sufficient; dropping it leaves the wrapper undecidable. const_0x3eb98 from the draft menu is not marked on-target because both format strings are already visible in the function body shown to the model (the str.* flag names), so it adds nothing new (dry-run rule 6). Off-path distractors are real callees of this function that do not build the command: 0x0001f192 is a config setter (request strings are persisted via WritePrivateProfileString, never run), and 0x0001f3ce opens the constant path /dev/null for output redirection. The upstream session check auth_get_session plus the administrators-group check User_Belongs_To_Group in appRequest.cgi main() (0x35fe8) gates this handler, so the requested command runs only for a request that already holds a valid, admin-group session.
